requirements.statement: On a germinal products notification's view header, no action shares another action's form: 'Copy as new' posts a form of its own, and 'Amend this notification' and Delete are links to their own confirmation pages placed outside it, as on the live animals header.
requirements.why: The 19 November ruling gives every posting button on the view header its own form and keeps Delete a link to its confirmation page; the 25 November ruling makes Amend a link to the amend confirmation page and applies the header rule to live animals, germinal products and plants alike. The germinal set's amend, copy and delete build on what the manage notifications theme lands (27 November ruling).
requirements.deltaNote: No germinal products set is walked or served today (repo-tests-p8-152), so the germinal copy of the view header is new.

requirements.statement: 'Amend this notification' on a notification's view header is a link to that notification's amend confirmation page, outside any other action's form, in the live animals, germinal products and plants frontends. Following it changes nothing: the notification moves into amendment only when the trader confirms on that page.
requirements.why: The 25 November ruling answers the header question: the first click on Amend changes nothing, a post that only renders a page is the wrong verb and leaves a re-post on the back button without JavaScript, and Delete already opens its confirmation page by link in the same header.
requirements.deltaNote: Today the live animals view header's Amend posts a form of its own and the post starts the amendment at once, taking the record to AMEND and writing the snapshots (ruling-ian-2026-11-25b-p1-008, ruling-ian-2026-11-25b-p1-010). Plants' amend moves behind the same confirmation page (ruling-sam-2026-10-09-pm-p3-057).

requirements.statement: A journey page is told where the trader came from by the trail the service writes into the page's own address: the places already saved, newest last, named in the service's own words (the dashboard, the overview, the Import Notification Service and the review page). The trail shortens by one as Back is followed, is dropped when it names a place the journey does not have, and carries through a page's own in-page actions.
requirements.why: The return and Back rules need a context the service can read on a page it serves by URL. The save and continue work that has since merged writes that trail in both frontends, which the 9 October ruling's wording did not foresee; whether it stays is an open question (c-451).
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p3-002, repo-tests-p8-005 and repo-tests-p8-012: a live animals journey page's address already carries the places the trader came by as a comma-separated trail, newest last, starting from the overview, the dashboard or the Import Notification Service; repo-plantsfrontend-p14-002 and repo-plantsfrontend-p14-016: plants carries the same trail and shortens it as Back is followed; repo-plantsfrontend-p14-109: a page opened straight by its address carries none.

requirements.statement: Each posting button on a notification's view header belongs to its own form, which the button names by the form's id rather than sitting inside it, so no action shares another's form; Delete is a link to the delete confirmation page, outside every form, in the live animals and the high-risk plants frontends.
requirements.why: The owner's 19 November ruling gives each posting button on the notification view header its own form, as every other posting button in the service has, and keeps Delete as a link to its confirmation page; the 25 November ruling keeps that rule while Amend becomes a link.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p3-105 and repo-plantsfrontend-p14-095: each posting control in the notification view's header belongs to a form it names by id rather than sitting inside it; repo-frontend-p3-057 and ruling-ian-2026-11-25b-p1-009: Delete opens a confirmation page of its own by link rather than posting from the header.

requirements.statement: A notification's status strip and status tag read one of 'Draft', 'Submitted', 'Amend', 'Cancel amend' or 'Deleted', and no status says an action is required: a notification submitted with items still outstanding, such as a missing health certificate, reads 'Submitted' like any other, and nothing action-required is shown on the notification view, the review page or the list. A notification whose every task is complete still reads 'Draft' until it is submitted.
requirements.why: The owner's 16 November ruling refuses a status that does not align with the notification flow, so outstanding actions wait for a banner the dashboard designs introduce, and 'Completed' stays out until a real source of completion exists.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-plantsfrontend-p14-094: the statuses plants' strip and tag show are Draft, Submitted, Amend, Cancel amend and Deleted; repo-frontend-p3-104: the live animals strip's statuses are Draft, Submitted, Amend and Deleted, with 'Cancel amend' the control that ends an amendment (repo-tests-p8-126); neither has an action-required status, and repo-frontend-p3-052: a complete draft's view reads Draft.

requirements.why: This is the question order the target design walks in every live animals journey, and the order the real service already walks; both frontends' suites and the tests repo hold the journey to it.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p3-121 and repo-tests-p8-157: Save and continue already carries a new notification from the origin page through these pages in this order, and repo-frontend-p3-123 checks each landing by its slug and heading.

requirements.statement: Starting a germinal products notification opens its Origin of the import page straight away, with no notification type question, and the notification is labelled Germinal products from that page onward.
requirements.why: The target design starts a germinal notification on its origin page once the category is known, and the germinal products set has its own journey, so it has no type question of its own.
requirements.deltaNote: No germinal products notification can be started or walked today (repo-tests-p8-152).

requirements.statement: A germinal products notification's opening run takes Save and continue through Origin of the import, What are you importing?, Main import reason, Commodity details, Total gross weight, Identification details, Arrival details, Transit countries when the consignment travels by rail or road, Transport details, Upload documents and Consignment addresses. It has no Additional details step, and once every task is done its overview has a Total gross weight row after Commodity details and no Additional details row. The total gross weight is held for each species.

requirements.deltaNote: No germinal products journey is served or walked today (repo-tests-p8-152).

requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p3-033, repo-tests-p8-008 and repo-tests-p8-009: today a road consignment's Save and continue opens transit countries and an air consignment's skips it to the transporter page.

A rail or road consignment has an eleventh row, Transit countries, between Arrival details and Transport details, and no other row is listed.

requirements.deltaNote: repo-tests-p8-070 and repo-tests-p8-071: the horse walk already runs from create to submitted on every supported browser, and repo-tests-p8-072 checks the main import reason card.

requirements.statement: The tests repo walks a germinal products notification for bovine semen from create to submitted in the germinal products set, in a spec under the animals Playwright project's germinal products folder, checking its overview has no Additional details row, its review shows the answers given and its confirmation shows the reference.

requirements.deltaNote: Every whole journey the tests repo walks today is a live animals one (repo-tests-p8-152).

requirements.statement: A live animals notification created from the set's own list and answered task by task from the overview, giving only the answers the service requires to submit, can be submitted through the review and the declaration to the confirmation page, and the tests repo proves it.
requirements.why: It proves that a trader can finish a notification without walking the opening run, and that the answers the service requires are exactly the ones it needs.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-tests-p8-168: the tests repo already submits a notification answered task by task from the overview with only the mandatory answers, on the compose stack.

requirements.statement: In a live animals journey, Back follows where the trader came from: the review reached by Save and continue from Consignment addresses goes back to Consignment addresses; a review opened by the overview's 'Review and submit' goes back to the overview; a submitted notification or an amendment opened from the set's own list goes back to that list, as does the review once an amendment is cancelled; a page opened from a review Change link goes back to the review, after a refresh and in a new session too; and a page Save and continue opened goes back to the page before it. Every Back link reads 'Back'.
requirements.why: A trader must be able to retrace a whole journey from wherever they entered it, and the target design's 'overall dashboard' is the set's own list in the real service.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-tests-p8-052 to repo-tests-p8-059 and repo-tests-p8-167: today's whole-journey Back specs prove each of these destinations, and repo-frontend-p3-077 and repo-frontend-p3-078 the reverse walk through the opening run.

requirements.statement: In the high-risk plants journey, Back on the commodities list, the arrival details, the identification numbers and the consignment contact pages opens the page the trader pressed Save and continue on, following the branch the commodity type opened; going back in the browser after following Back returns to the step the trader was on; and pressing Save and continue on a page reached by Back carries the trader on to the next step rather than stopping there.
requirements.why: Plants mirrors the live animals Back behaviour on its own step order, and its fit suite proves it on whole walks.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-plantsfrontend-p14-013 to repo-plantsfrontend-p14-019: plants' fit suite already proves these Back destinations on ware potato, seed potato and wood walks.

requirements.statement: A signed-in trader can take a high-risk plants notification from the dashboard through plants' own step order, its check your answers, its declaration and its confirmation, and plants' fit suite proves it for five use cases: ware potatoes from Spain notified before arrival, ware potatoes from Portugal notified after arrival, seed potatoes from the Netherlands, spruce from Germany with species and EPPO code, and conifer wood without bark from Italy with phytosanitary treatments. A late notification's confirmation shows the late heading and an on-time one does not, and each confirmation passes the accessibility check.
requirements.why: Plants shares the journey engine, check your answers, declaration and confirmation, so a change to any of them must keep plants' whole walk working.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-plantsfrontend-p14-001: plants' journey smoke spec already walks these five use cases from the dashboard to confirmation, and repo-plantsfrontend-p14-110 and repo-plantsfrontend-p14-011 check the late heading.

requirements.statement: A page opened from a review page Change link keeps the trader on the way back to the review through its own in-page actions and posts, such as removing an animal or adding a document, until it is left by its own Save and continue; there the animal identification page offers Save and continue rather than Save and add another, and an answer changed this way shows on the review afterwards.
requirements.why: A trader correcting one answer from the review must not lose their place, and the change must reach what they are about to submit.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p3-081 to repo-frontend-p3-084 and repo-frontend-p3-131: the frontend's journey smoke spec already proves this from the notification view.

requirements.statement: Every journey page that collects answers ends with a 'Save and continue' button and a 'Save and return to overview' button together in one button group, the second the form's last button, with a 'Cancel and return to overview' link below the group; a page reached from outside a notification ends with its primary button and a cancel link back to the set's list instead. This holds in the live animals, germinal products and plants journeys.
requirements.why: Both frontends and the tests repo hold every journey page to the same set of save controls, so a trader can always save and leave or leave without saving.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-frontend-p3-060 and repo-plantsfrontend-p14-056: both frontends' journey pages already show the three controls in this order and grouping, and repo-tests-p8-061 asserts it.

requirements.statement: Every reference-list field a journey asks (the country of origin, the transit country, the transit and transhipment destination countries, the port of entry and both ports of exit) is an accessible autocomplete that enhances a native select of the same name: with JavaScript off the trader uses the select, with it on they type and pick a suggestion, and the field offers the same entries either way and keeps the chosen entry when the page is reopened.
requirements.why: Every page works fully without JavaScript, and a search box uses the real frontend's accessible autocomplete over a native select.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-tests-p8-122 and repo-frontend-p3-012: today each reference-list field is an accessible autocomplete over a native select, and repo-tests-p8-099 and repo-tests-p8-101 prove the country lists offer the same entries with JavaScript on and off.

requirements.statement: The k6 performance suite drives a live animals draft through the journey by the set's own page slugs and form field names: origin, commodities (a search then the species), import-reason, consignment-details, commodities/identification, additional-details, the documents, addresses and the five party pickers, cph-number, port-of-entry, transit-countries and transporters, reopening and resaving answered pages and amending a submitted notification's origin; every save lands on a page that answers 200 with no redirect loop and no stale-save redirect. A row that renames a slug or a field the suite posts changes the suite in the same increment.
requirements.why: The suite proves the journey holds up under load. The journey's URL paths and field names stay the real service's, and the suite changes in each increment whose change breaks one of its k6 scripts (c-225); the reframed notification list stays at the live-animals set root, so the suite's list request does not move.
requirements.deltaNote: repo-perftests-p3-001 and repo-perftests-p3-003: the k6 walker already fills a live animals draft in these 12 steps and checks each save lands on a 200 page; repo-perftests-p3-080 and repo-perftests-p3-081 reopen and amend.

requirements.statement: The target design's prototype mechanics and demonstration data are not built: the /design-release-2.1 path prefix, the prototype's reference pattern and generator, the submitted view's fixed sample answers shown under any new reference, form posts held only inside the prototype with no backend, and the demo answers, transporters and address book entries its journeys pick. Nor are its display quirks: a date shown exactly as typed, the region code joined to a prefix the trader never typed, a transporter's country repeated on its last address line, town, postcode and country joined onto one address line, 'United Kingdom' added to a new permanent address with no country, and a new permanent address's email and phone left off every display.
requirements.why: The prototype decides look and feel, never architecture, and its app/data fixtures are evidence of nothing but what it hard-coded; these quirks come from the prototype's own storage and demo data rather than from anything the real service's model needs.

requirements.statement: Reference-list content is not edited to match the target design or the tests: which countries, territories and ports the lists hold, their names, codes, order and spelling (the 31 origin countries and 9 subdivisions, the 78 ports in airports-seaports-rail order, the doubled 'Pembroke Port' and 'Port of Sheerness', 'Teestort', 'TILBURY', 'Portsmouth  Port', a port's code with or without a space, a port named two ways, the species' Latin names), and which import reasons, purposes, certification purposes, means of transport and transporters the demo lists offer.
requirements.why: Reference-list content is whatever MDM serves through reference-data and is never edited in code; field values the notification captures come from the data specification, never from the prototype's or a test suite's fixtures. The served oddities go to MDM as a data-quality report.

requirements.statement: Claims in this area that describe one page's own content, data or rules are weighed in that page's own area rather than here: the notification type question and the start button; the origin, commodities, commodity details, identification, additional details, arrival, transit countries, transporter, upload documents, consignment addresses, party picker, CPH number and permanent address pages' questions, copy, buttons and save rules; the overview's commodity totals and save-and-return behaviour; the review page's title, heading, sections, cards, rows, tables, labels and Change and Delete controls; the submitted view's header, title, Actions, Make template, Copy buttons and import reference numbers; the declaration's statements, checkbox, error and date; the confirmation's panel, sections, inspection-stay bullets and links; the entry guard and what a page may save blank; page titles, captions, the service navigation, error summaries, date pickers, search boxes, layout and accessibility checks; and plants' own pages, labels, pickers and confirmation copy.
requirements.why: Each page keeps its own content in its own area, and step order and scope rules stay with the journey flow area, so the builder finds one requirement per difference where that page is specified.

requirements.statement: The suites' fixture data and driving mechanics are test scaffolding, not requirements: the stub sign-in route and organisation ids, the fresh-organisation trick, Playwright projects, timeouts and recording settings, seeded draft stages and the pages a seeded draft posts to, the canned transporters, document files and address book records, the named happy-path answers, reposting a form with fields replaced or an option added, rewritten radios, computed arrival dates, the trail and reference matchers, style probes, run-recorded notifications, and the k6 walker's blank-field answers, select defaults, skipped search boxes, worst-case search, endpoint tags, hidden-field repost and body encoding.
requirements.why: These exist to drive and check the services; they describe no behaviour a trader, an operator or another system observes.

requirements.statement: What the whole-journey sources do not show is recorded, not built: how the target design returns from Save and return to overview, a second species or a review Change link, what its review Delete and its submitted view's Amend, Make template, Copy as new and Delete do, a submitted horse or chicken view with its own answers, hub statuses between To do and Complete, the declaration date's format, whether a germinal notification can have a permanent address, CPH number or contact address, what the submitted page sends onward, which pages beyond three the caption and title specs cover, where the Address book, Manage account and Log out items lead, what a page does when the stub address book or reference data cannot be reached, the frontend smoke spec's submission, amendment and deletion, a transporter added, a party edited, a notification deleted or an amendment cancelled inside a whole walk, a documented page order in the tests repo, hints and placeholders on the reference lists, the dashboard beyond the actions the walks use, plants' amend and copy, and any wording the k6 scripts read.
requirements.why: A gap in the evidence is not a requirement; each is weighed where its page or behaviour is specified.

conflicts.about: How a task list heading is spelled: the prototype's one-word 'tasklist', or the two-word GOV.UK spelling.

positions.says: The notification task list heading reads 'Notification task list'.
'task list' is spelled as two words, which is the GOV.UK spelling.
The overview's task list is a region named 'Notification task list', with the tasks grouped under numbered sections.

conflicts.outcome: The owner's decision of 19 November ranks first and names 'task list', two words, as the GOV.UK spelling of the heading. Its reason is the spelling itself rather than the one page it was given on, so a notification's task list is headed 'Notification task list' and a template's 'Template task list', and one service does not spell the same heading two ways. The prototype's one-word 'tasklist', which this area's working set no longer carries and the overview and templates areas weigh, is set aside; the tests repo's whole walks already read the two-word heading. No claim is overruled.

conflicts.about: Whether a journey page's context is carried as the trail the service now writes in the page's address, or as the ?change=1 flag and no trail that the 9 October ruling kept

positions.says: The amend controls keep their content with no action field; exit=hub and ?change=1 stay.
No ?from=hub marker is added; only the live flow's fallback changes.
The return links are treated as blocked, waiting on the save and continue theme, and build once that work has merged.
A journey page's URL may carry a from= query holding the trail of pages the trader came through.
A journey page's address carries the places the trader came by as a from= query, newest last, with the overview, the dashboard and the Import Notification Service as its starting places.
Every journey page's address carries a trail of the places the trader has saved before it.

conflicts.outcome: Unsettled, and the two readings build different services. The 9 October ruling kept ?change=1 and added no marker, and on its plain reading the trail that the save and continue work has since merged into both frontends comes out and the review context goes back to ?change=1. The other reading is that how a service remembers where a trader came from is its own architecture, which the ruling described rather than decided, and that the 10 November ruling deferred the return links to exactly that merged work; the trail then stays and the return and Back rules are specified against it. Precedence ranks neither, because the later ruling defers to the work that built the trail while the earlier one names the flag, and the 27 November ruling settles only the germinal questions, not this one, so the question goes to the owner. Nothing about where a saved page or a Back link goes turns on the answer: the Back and return requirements state those destinations without naming the mechanism.
conflicts.question: Does the journey keep the trail it now writes into each page's address as the way it remembers where a trader came from, or come off it and go back to the ?change=1 flag with no trail?
conflicts.default: The trail stays, in both frontends. A page's address carries the places already saved, newest last, in the service's own names; the review context is the review page's own place on that trail instead of ?change=1; and no page of the merged save and continue work is reverted. New work specifies the return and Back rules by where the trader came from rather than by the query that records it.

conflicts.about: Whether a horse journey's additional details page asks the unweaned animals question: the prototype's horse walk shows none, while today's horse walk answers it.

positions.says: No row may rest on the prototype's demo data for which commodities a rule covers; the data specification says it.
The horse journey answers additional details with one choice and shows no unweaned animals question.
A horse consignment's additional details card holds 'Certified for' and 'Includes unweaned animals', showing Registered equine animal and No.

conflicts.outcome: The 11 November ruling ranks first: which commodities the unweaned animals question covers is the data specification's 'Contains Unweaned Animals' list, never what the prototype's demo journey happened to show for a horse. The horse shape is asked the question exactly when that list names the horse commodity; the list itself is weighed with the additional details page. The prototype's horse reading is set aside as a rule. The tests repo's horse walk stands as evidence of today and changes only if the list leaves the horse out.

conflicts.about: Where Save and continue on Consignment addresses goes once every task is complete: the overview, as the target design walks, or the draft review, as the real journey does today.

positions.says: Save and continue on a completed Consignment addresses page goes to the notification hub.
Save and continue on Consignment addresses goes to the notification hub, ending the opening run.
Once every party and the CPH number are added, Save and continue on Consignment addresses opens the notification view as a draft.
Pressing Continue on Consignment addresses, the last question page, lands the trader on the review page.

conflicts.outcome: The target design ranks above the real repos and decides the journey's question order and where its steps lead; what the real service does today is not on its own a reason to depart from it. A complete notification's Consignment addresses therefore saves to the overview, where every row reads Complete and 'Review and submit' opens the review. The design walks only complete notifications, so an incomplete one still ends its opening run on the draft review that names what is outstanding. No claim is overruled: the today claims still back the incomplete case and the absence of a contact address step.
